strengths: Proposes a well-structured multi-dimensional benchmark (Fidelity, Expressiveness, Aesthetics) targeting the underexplored problem of visualization quality assessment.
Comprehensive dataset construction comprising 3,090 samples across 32 chart categories, supported by a rigorous multi-stage annotation and expert adjudication workflow.
Demonstrates clear downstream utility by applying VisJudge as an evaluation and reward model to improve chart generation and recommendation frameworks.
weaknesses: Data fidelity assessment is restricted to visually apparent cues rather than ground-truth tabular data verification, limiting the detection of subtle numerical inaccuracies.
The adaptive question and rubric generation pipeline relies heavily on GPT-4o, which may introduce systemic prompt biases across the benchmark.
The scope is restricted to static visualization images, leaving out interactive and dynamic visual analytics scenarios.

strengths: Addresses an underexplored and practically relevant problem by formalizing visualization evaluation into Fidelity, Expressiveness, and Aesthetics.
Comprehensive dataset construction covering 3,090 samples across single views, multi-views, and dashboards, supported by a structured quality control and expert validation workflow.
Extensive empirical evaluation across multiple proprietary and open-source MLLMs, clearly diagnosing specific failure modes such as score inflation.
Effective demonstration of practical utility by integrating the fine-tuned model into visualization generation and recommendation pipelines.
weaknesses: Inclusion of unpublished or unverified models (e.g., GPT-5) raises reproducibility concerns and complicates baseline comparisons.
Heavy reliance on GPT-4o for metadata extraction and evaluation question rewriting risks introducing proprietary model biases into the benchmark rubrics.
Subjectivity remains high across aesthetic dimensions, and algorithmic outlier filtering during crowd annotation may inadvertently smooth out legitimate human preference variance.

The training formulation with GRPO relies primarily on absolute error penalization against scalar labels, which functions similarly to supervised regression without deeply exploring preference ranking.

strengths: Introduces a multi-dimensional taxonomy covering Data Fidelity, Expressiveness, and Visual Aesthetics across diverse visualization types.
Comprehensive benchmark construction featuring 3,090 real-world samples with structured crowdsourced annotation and expert review pipelines.
Demonstrates downstream utility of the fine-tuned VisJudge model in iterative visualization generation and recommendation tasks.
weaknesses: Data fidelity is evaluated solely from visual appearance without access to underlying tabular data, limiting conclusive verification of data accuracy.
The modeling contribution relies on standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) and RL (GRPO) without visualization-specific architectural innovations.
Subjective variance remains inherent in aesthetic scoring, and the evaluation relies heavily on synthetic rubric adaptations generated via LLM prompting.

strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored problem by benchmarking multimodal foundation models on multi-dimensional visualization quality (fidelity, expressiveness, and aesthetics).
Introduces a substantial dataset of 3,090 diverse real-world visualization samples spanning single views, multi-views, and dashboards.
Implements a thorough annotation pipeline that combines crowdsourced ratings, statistical anomaly detection, and expert adjudication.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on GPT-4o for adaptive question generation, metadata extraction, and semantic filtering may introduce systematic synthetic biases into the benchmark.
The evaluation of model-generated textual rationales is primarily qualitative, lacking systematic quantitative assessment against human explanations.
The fine-tuned VisJudge model is trained and tested on splits from the same crawled corpus, leaving cross-dataset generalization unproven.

strengths: Well-motivated benchmark targeting visualization quality assessment across three grounded dimensions: Fidelity, Expressiveness, and Aesthetics.
Comprehensive dataset comprising 3,090 samples spanning single charts, multi-view visualizations, and dashboards across 32 subtypes.
Rigorous data curation and multi-stage annotation process involving crowdsourcing filters and visualization expert adjudication.
Extensive benchmarking of prominent MLLMs revealing systematic failure modes, such as score inflation and weak aesthetic appraisal.
Effective application of reinforcement learning (GRPO) on Qwen2.5-VL to align model predictions closer to human expert judgments.
weaknesses: Model fine-tuning and evaluation are confined to splits of the same collected corpus, leaving cross-dataset and out-of-domain generalizability untested.
The reward formulation directly optimizes numerical score proximity, but the quality, faithfulness, and fluency of the generated rationales are not quantitatively evaluated.
Formal inter-annotator reliability metrics (such as Krippendorff's alpha or Fleiss' kappa) prior to expert reconciliation are not reported.

strengths: Proposes a well-structured and timely benchmark (VisJudge-Bench) comprising 3,090 diverse visualization samples spanning single views, multi-views, and dashboards across 32 chart types.
Establishes a grounded evaluation framework decomposing visualization quality into Fidelity, Expressiveness, and Aesthetics with detailed rubrics and adaptive prompt templates.
Employs a rigorous multi-stage annotation and quality control workflow combining crowdsourced screening, algorithmic anomaly detection, and expert adjudication.
Demonstrates the utility of the benchmark as training data, showing that fine-tuning with reinforcement learning (VisJudge) yields measurable alignment gains over general MLLMs.
weaknesses: Includes references to unreleased commercial systems (such as GPT-5 and Claude-4-Sonnet) without providing concrete provenance, access details, or reproducibility documentation.
Lacks ablation experiments comparing the GRPO reinforcement learning setup against standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or direct regression baselines.
Aesthetic dimensions remain inherently subjective, and evaluation does not fully characterize inter-annotator variance or out-of-distribution human perceptual agreement.
